Self-Custody & Sovereign Infrastructure

When the App Goes Offline: Sovereign Exits and Rebuilt Hatches

Blitz releases an open-source recovery tool, self-hosters benchmark UmbrelOS 2.0, and developers push back against walled ecosystems with sovereign infrastructure.

By Our Technology Desk

When a Bitcoin wallet expands into multiple accounts, pools, and savings goals, self-custody faces an uncomfortable test: what happens if the company’s servers disappear tomorrow?

In an ecosystem that prizes sovereign control of funds, convenience frequently drifts toward invisible dependencies. That tension came into focus today as Blitz Wallet unveiled a completely rebuilt and open-source emergency escape hatch. As the developers put it, Blitz offers more than a single wallet. With separate allocations for gifts, pools, accounts, and savings goals, how do you reach all of it without the Blitz app?

Their answer is a standalone recovery utility built specifically for catastrophic scenarios: Fully open source and built for the case where Blitz goes offline. Because it leverages off-chain state through Spark, the team took care to delineate its trust boundaries: It uses the Spark network, so it is not a unilateral exit tool. Users seeking access can reach the standalone tool at recover.blitzwalletapp.com (Blitz Wallet).

The impulse toward local resilience resonated widely across the network. Reviewing recent developments on local hardware, NostrLlama reported on the latest Raspberry Pi release of Umbrel: After checking out UmbrelOS 2.0 on my Pi yesterday, I'm really considering also buying the Umbrel hardware to self-host basically anything (NostrLlama). They noted how far self-hosted systems have evolved from early hobbyist builds, observing that the UX/UI is so polished and functional now.

Meanwhile, peer-to-peer exchange RoboSats affirmed its deepening reliance on open protocols rather than closed server architecture, reminding traders: RoboSats has integrated Nostr for many features and keeps adding more of them. (RoboSats).

Privacy & Civil Liberties

Surveillance Threats in Europe as Russia Splits the Net

German digital rights advocates sound the alarm on Chatkontrolle 2.0, while human rights monitors report on state internet manipulation.

By Our Privacy Correspondent

A critical battle over personal encryption is brewing in Brussels. Former MEP and digital rights advocate Patrick Breyer issued an urgent warning to European citizens ahead of a crucial vote early next week: Dienstag droht schmutziger Deal zur #Chatkontrolle 2.0 mit PERMANENTER Erlaubnis von Massenscans unserer privaten Chats (Patrick Breyer). The proposal would establish permanent mandates for mass client-side scanning of private messaging applications across member states.

The precarious state of communication freedom was underscored globally by the Human Rights Foundation’s Financial Freedom Report #139, which documented how authoritarian regimes manipulate connectivity: organizers of an international youth festival reportedly created multiple versions of the internet (HRF), offering uncensored web access on tailored SIM cards to foreign visitors while keeping domestic citizens behind rigid national firewalls.

Exchanges & Scams

Suspected $352M Bitget Drain; KYCnot.me Blacklists Swapter

Security desks tracked massive abnormal outflows from centralised exchange Bitget overnight: Nearly $352M Moved From Crypto Exchange Bitget Wallets in Suspected Hack (Bitcoin Magazine), renewing scrutiny on custodial counterparty risks.

Simultaneously, privacy watchdog KYCnot.me issued an unsparing notice regarding swap platform Swapter: We have marked Swapter as a scam. The watchdog documented predatory behavior against customers: Large swaps are held for months and never paid or refunded (KYCnot.me), even after users provided identity documents and proofs of funds.

On a brighter note for circular spending, Coincards announced its third major platform overhaul: Spend Bitcoin like cash. The service highlighted instant settlement without intermediaries: Gift cards for your favourite stores, Pay with Bitcoin or Lightning, and No bank required (Coincards.com).

Despatches & Community

Mascots & Feeds

The Search for a Mascot, and Reclaiming Social Feeds

A lighthearted Friday debate over protocol symbolism turned into a broader discussion on community identity. If you had to choose a new nostr mascot, what would it be? asked Joe Martin (Joe Martin), putting forward the Elephant seal. A.A.Ron countered with an aquatic nomination: Electric eel, because they zap and are kinda cute. (A.A.Ron).

Martin struck a more earnest tone reflecting on algorithmic feeds versus decentralized networks, creating curated follower packs for musicians: Social media used to be about connection with friends and now it's about consumption driven by surveillance capitalism. (Joe Martin).

North of Morocco by Train; Hand-Knotted Silk

Travel notes arrived from North Africa, where Jurjen de Vries checked in from regional rails: Traveling with my backpack in the north of Morocco. (Jurjen de Vries). En route between historic cities, he noted: Have visited Assilah, Larache and Rabat, going by train to Meknes this afternoon.
